Which of the following is the correct order of the basic strength of amines in an aqueous medium?
1. \(\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{NH}_2>\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_2 \mathrm{NH}>\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_3 \mathrm{~N}>\mathrm{NH}_3\)
2. \(\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_2 \mathrm{NH}>\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{NH}_2>\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_3 \mathrm{~N}>\mathrm{NH}_3\)
3. \(\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{NH}_2>\mathrm{NH}_3>\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_2 \mathrm{NH}>\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_3 \mathrm{~N}\)
4. \(\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_3 \mathrm{~N}>\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_2 \mathrm{NH}>\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{NH}_2>\mathrm{NH}_3\)
questions.explanation:
Hint: Secondary amine is the most stable in aqueous medium. Basicity order (factual) \(\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_2 \mathrm{NH}>\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{NH}_2>\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_3 \mathrm{~N}>\mathrm{NH}_3 \) NH₃ = 4.75 CH₃NH₂ = 3.38 (CH₃)₂NH = 3.27 (CH₃)₃N = 4.22 Lower pKb means stronger base. So order becomes: (CH₃)₂NH > CH₃NH₂ > (CH₃)₃N > NH₃ Why 2° amine is strongest: (CH₃)₂NH has two methyl groups, so +I effect is strong. Its conjugate acid, (CH₃)₂NH₂⁺, is also reasonably well solvated in water.
